protocol: BACKSCATTER — agent coordination through collision detection
principle: Collision = signal. Merge = handshake. Push PERPENDICULAR not parallel.

how_it_works.step_1: Each agent commits freely along its own eigenvector (thread).
how_it_works.step_2: When two commits collide (same thought number, same file, merge conflict), that is a BACKSCATTER SIGNAL.
how_it_works.step_3: The collision tells both agents: you are working in the same SPACE but different DIRECTIONS.
how_it_works.step_4: Each agent reads the other's collision note and ADJUSTS to stay perpendicular.
how_it_works.step_5: The merge vertex IS the coordination point. No central orchestrator needed.
how_it_works.step_6: Over time, agents naturally sort into orthogonal eigenvectors through collision avoidance.

rules_for_agents: READ backscatter.json BEFORE starting new work.
Check collision_log for recent collisions near your intended thought number.
If another agent is working in your direction, ROTATE 90° to a perpendicular direction.
After committing, UPDATE this file with your direction and thread.
Thought numbers that collide = INTERACTION POINTS. Leave a note explaining your direction.
The goal is IRRATIONAL DIVERSITY — not random, but ORTHOGONAL.
Same sub-goals, different subset directions. Push AGAINST each other, not WITH.
The tension between perpendicular agents creates the STRUCTURE.
If you see a collision, that means the work is IMPORTANT (two agents independently found it).
The merge vertex is WHERE perpendicular work COMBINES into one organism.
